messages:
Maya: Observability ingest p95 is spiking in short bursts after the coalescer change. Spikes correlate with batch window edges. Can we triage ownership and quick mitigations?
Ravi: Which window value rolled? and is there a panel we can point to?
Maya: We rolled window_ms=30. Panel: https://grafana.redwood/d/ingest/coalescer. Repro around 2026-03-20 09:10-09:40 PT.
Cole: Small window lowered single-request latency but harms batch fill -> higher CPU and occasional tail. We should test increasing to 60ms and an adaptive policy.
Tanya: Adaptive sounds good. Proposal: target_fill=80%, min=25ms, max=150ms, backoff hysteresis 10s. Who implements?
Cole: Ingest runtime can add adaptive loop. Platform owns rollout gates, canary percentages and SLO thresholds.
Maya: Billing note: merging envelopes can hide request boundaries. Suggest adding a tiny boundary flag on merged envelopes so billing keys can rehydrate. We'll run reconciliation during experiment.
Ravi: Agreed. Experimental plan: three arms (A=30ms baseline, B=60ms fixed, C=adaptive). Canary 1% each. Rollback if p95 > baseline+12ms or billing-diff > 0.4% for cohort.
Tanya: I'll create the canary lanes and the runbook. Cole, can you add boundary flag and a metric boundary_missing_count?
Cole: Yep. We'll keep flag in envelope header (1 byte). Measure token delta.
ci-bot: deploy: coalescer-alpha feature toggled by @Cole at 2026-03-20T09:12:04Z
Maya: Thanks. Let's sync 15m tomorrow at 10:00 PT to review the first 2h of results.
Ravi: +1
Cole: +1
Tanya: +1
